name: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Benchmarks multimodal agents on data-science and engineering workflows involving enterprise applications, code, and GUI operations in real computer environments.

name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
notes: The paper abstract and official full-text sections were reviewed. The full text supports Windows 11 virtual-machine execution, screenshot/state observations, and mouse/keyboard actions. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LabOSBench evaluates GUI agents on browser-based scientific instrument simulators with configurable tasks and execution-based checks. Its subtask and end-to-end tests examine feedback-driven adjustment and long workflows without controlling physical instruments.

name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
notes: The paper abstract and official project README were reviewed. The README documents an Ubuntu desktop and GUI action interface and includes LLM-assisted evaluators; this annotation does not assert that every evaluator is deterministic. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.

name: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces professional engineering tasks across software domains, with GUI and CLI access and artifact checks for geometric, physical, and design validity.

name: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Benchmarks computer agents on scientific-software workflows with task-specific checks of application states and generated research artifacts.

name: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Evaluates GUI agents in simulated medical-imaging consoles, separately checking workflow completion and acquisition outcomes against hidden anatomical targets.

This profile covers the released VM task definitions; Docker smoke results and Raw/Dual alternatives are separate populations.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Manifest count 169 matches the official verifier audit. Other Raw/Dual definitions can represent alternative execution modes of the same problems and are not added. Official Docker migration documents a 20-task acceptance subset, not a full-suite performance result; legacy VMware remains. External service sign-in/rate limits, amd64 binaries and ChimeraX redistribution terms limit portability. Only code MIT is established; VM, scientific data and bundled apps need their own terms.
